Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing assertion is the last one in RandomStringUtilsTest.testExceptions(), which expects RandomStringUtils.random(1, new char[0]) to throw an IllegalArgumentException.

Call flow and behavior:
- random(1, new char[0]) delegates to random(count, 0, chars.length, false, false, chars, RANDOM) in RandomStringUtils.random(int, char...) (lines 317–322). With an empty array, start=0 and end=0.
- In random(int, int, int, boolean, boolean, char[], Random) (lines 223–281):
  - The count checks are correct: count == 0 returns "", count < 0 throws IllegalArgumentException (lines 225–229). This is why the first three try/catch blocks in the test succeed.
  - For the empty array case: since start == 0 and end == 0, the code enters the block at lines 231–238. Because letters and numbers are both false, end is set to Integer.MAX_VALUE while start remains 0 (lines 232–237).
  - gap becomes end - start = Integer.MAX_VALUE (line 241).
  - In the loop, because chars != null, the code executes ch = chars[random.nextInt(gap) + start] (lines 245–249). With chars.length == 0, any index into chars is invalid, resulting in an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
- Thus, instead of throwing IllegalArgumentException for an empty char array (as the test requires), the method attempts to index into the empty array and throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

Relation to the issue report:
- The current bug report states that random(count, 0, 0, false, false, universe, random) throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when end is 0 or when the array is empty. This matches exactly what happens: the code mistakenly treats the (start==0 && end==0) case as a signal to generate from a range even when a non-null chars array is provided, leading to indexing into an empty array.
- The suggested workaround in the report (using modulo by chars.length) would avoid AIOOBE but would not satisfy the test’s requirement that providing an empty character array should be illegal. The correct behavior per the test is to detect and reject an empty chars array with IllegalArgumentException.

Root cause:
- Missing validation for an empty chars array, combined with logic that overrides end when start==0 && end==0 even when chars != null. This leads to an attempt to index into an empty array and an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, violating the API contract expected by the tests.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

RandomStringUtils.random(int, char...)
RandomStringUtils.random(int, int, int, boolean, boolean, char[], java.util.Random)
